about: Written reasons for open security alerts that are fixed but not yet scanned, by design, false positives, or waiting for an upstream release. Checked by scripts/security-response-check.mjs; see docs/security/vulnerability-response.md. Nobody dismisses alerts on GitHub from here.

alerts.reason: Real bug fixed in #565: the escape replaced a text with itself, so Unicode line separators were not escaped in .env.local. The alert closes once the fix reaches main and is scanned.

Reads package.json inside the user's own data folder to recognise an older FLUJO checkout. Anyone who can swap that file can already change the user's data; the worst case is a wrong yes or no answer.
The id is used as a key in a new object literal ({ [id]: value }). A computed key in a literal always creates an own property, so it cannot change the object prototype.

Installing a package runs the install and build commands the person reviewed in the install wizard; that is the feature. Since #565 the install refuses a package that differs from the reviewed one (reviewDigest) and installs the reviewed version, so only reviewed commands run.

The Docker program path comes from the owner-approved isolation policy, and the launch is refused unless the private owner approval file holds the exact policy digest. Since #565 only a program named docker or docker.exe is accepted, and arguments are passed without a shell.

Development only (Jest, typescript-eslint and coverage tools); patterns come from our own config files, not from users. The newest Jest 30.5.2 and test-exclude 8.0.0 still need minimatch 10 and glob 13. The fixed minimatch 11 and glob 14 change their matching API, so forcing them could break the test runner. Revisit when Jest moves to glob 14.
